RaMP ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR = 3.11e-15 and fold-enrichment = 2001.5, hitting five input metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5(S)-HETE, 15(S)-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2, and leukotriene A4) out of 27 pathway members. Mummichog, which maps by compound mass and does not require annotation, ranks Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top MUMM: pathway (p = 0.000168) with all five core eicosanoid inputs detected including the 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid (5,6-EET). The three non-eicosanoid inputs — 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid — are not enriched in any pathway across any paradigm, suggesting they are peripheral or incidental metabolites. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct — converge on a single biological domain: arachidonic acid eicosanoid metabolism. RaMP ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR = 3.11e-15 and fold-enrichment = 2001.5, hitting five input metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5(S)-HETE, 15(S)-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2, and leukotriene A4) out of 27 pathway members. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returns KEGG:hsa00590 (arachidonic acid metabolism) as the sole significant hit at p = 2.49e-06, with the same four eicosanoid intermediates (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15(S)-HETE, 5(S)-HETE). Mummichog, which maps by compound mass and does not require annotation, ranks Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top MUMM: pathway (p = 0.000168) with all five core eicosanoid inputs detected including the 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid (5,6-EET). The three non-eicosanoid inputs — 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid — are not enriched in any pathway across any paradigm, suggesting they are peripheral or incidental metabolites. Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the upstream substrate for the entire eicosanoid cascade; the three detected HETEs (5-HETE, 15-HETE) and leukotriene A4 are generated by distinct enzymatic branches (5-lipoxygenase and 15-lipoxygenase pathways), while 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 arises from the cyclopentenone prostaglandin branch. The convergence across ORA and network-based paradigms — with no competing significant hits — defines the treatment effect as a coordinated perturbation of the arachidonic acid eicosanoid synthesis network, with arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE and leukotriene A4 as the primary driver metabolites.
